The image displays a field of soybean plants, some of which exhibit yellowing on their leaves, particularly noticeable on the younger, uppermost leaves. The veins of these yellowed leaves appear to remain green, indicating interveinal chlorosis.

Comparing this visual evidence with the provided symptom descriptions, the most fitting match is "Iron_Deficiency_Chlorosis". The description for Iron Deficiency Chlorosis states: "Symptoms appear first on the youngest (top) leaves with yellow coloration between green veins (interveinal chlorosis), while older trifoliolate leaves remain entirely green." This aligns perfectly with the visual cues in the test image.

Other diseases like "Potassium_Deficiency" or "Sudden_Death_Syndrome" have some overlapping symptoms but do not precisely match the interveinal chlorosis on young leaves that is so prominent in the image. For example, Potassium Deficiency primarily affects leaf margins, and SDS has distinct root and stem symptoms not visible here.
